about: How a city's offense label becomes one of four buckets for Footing's local-safety signal. Rules are tried in order; the first regex (case-insensitive) that matches wins. Written 2026-10-24 from the offense lists Norfolk (data.norfolk.gov r7bn-2egr) and Charlottesville (gisweb.charlottesville.org OpenData_2/6) actually publish.

why.violent: Crimes against a person in public: assault, robbery, sexual assault, abduction, homicide, shootings, threats. This is the safety signal.
why.property: Theft of or damage to belongings: larceny, burglary, vehicle theft, vandalism, arson. Matters to someone whose belongings are with them.
why.enforcement: Trespass, disorderly conduct, drunkenness, loitering, drugs, warrants, mental-health custody calls. These measure where police make contact, not danger, and they are concentrated where unhoused people already are. Shown separately as a 'chance of being moved along' signal; never counted as danger.
why.other: Household and domestic offenses (they happen inside homes and say little about a public place), assaults on officers, fraud and paperwork crimes, shoplifting (store theft, not risk to a person), traffic, deaths, missing persons, lost property, animal calls. Not used.
